title: "Breaking the Game" - A pilot study on the acceptance of a digital offer for young people with problematic computer game behavior
summary:
Many teenagers and young adults play digital games regularly. However, some find it difficult to control their gaming time. This can lead to problems in everyday life, for example at school, in their social environment, or in family life. At the same time, people affected by computer game disorder or those showing early symptoms often shy away from seeking help from the healthcare system and look for self-help on the internet instead. However, there are currently only a few digital services that are specifically tailored to young people and have been tested for effectiveness.

“Breaking the Game” was developed to fill this gap. It is an anonymous digital service accessible via an internet browser that is aimed at young people who may be showing symptoms of computer game disorder, are avoiding seeking help from the healthcare system, and are looking for help on the internet. It provides basic information on how problematic gaming behavior can develop and encourages users to rethink their own usage behavior. Users are also encouraged to seek help from an addiction counseling center if necessary. The aim is to prevent problematic gaming behavior from becoming more severe or persisting over a longer period of time. The content is conveyed through texts, comics, and interactive elements. Among other things, it deals with how excessive gaming can develop, how personal goals can be taken into account more strongly again, how feelings can be better perceived and controlled, and what role social contacts play. 

The pilot study aims to gather initial information on how adolescents and young adults evaluate and accept “Breaking the Game.” It will also examine whether the planned study design is suitable for conducting a larger scientific study at a later date.

The study is open to adolescents and young adults between the ages of 12 and 25 who feel they have difficulty controlling their gaming behavior and who are not undergoing treatment or counseling on media use at the start of the study. Parents can also participate in surveys if they wish.

At the beginning of the study, the adolescents and young adults take part in a short online survey to check whether the conditions for participation are met. If these conditions are met, a more detailed survey follows. Only then are the participants randomly assigned to one of two groups. One group is given immediate access to “Breaking the Game” for eight weeks. The other group will wait eight weeks and only receive access after completing another survey.

Before and after this usage or waiting period, all participants will complete online questionnaires. During the eight-week usage period, they will also provide brief feedback on their usage behavior and playing time once a week. The entire study is anonymous and completely digital, and participation can be terminated at any time.

interventions.name: Intervention group:  “Breaking the Game” as self-learning training for 8 weeks
Waiting-control group: passive control group (intervention only after the waiting period has ended and the post-survey has been completed)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Age between 12 and 25 years. 
2. Consent of the patient and, if applicable, the parents. 
3. Exceeding a cut-off in the Gaming Disorder Scale for Adolescents (GADIS-A; Paschke, Austermann & Thomasius, 2020).
Exclusion criteria:
1. Previous experience with “Breaking the Game” (self-disclosure)
2. Parallel treatment of GD at Baseline
